1. The petitioner herein is seeking the relief in the nature of mandamus commanding the respondents to hold and declare that the award dated 10.3.2017 for village Umbhel, Taluka Kamrej,
District Surat passed by the competent officer/ Special Land Acquisition Officer in connection with the acquisition of the land-in-question is illegal and unconstitutional and further to pay additional compensation to the petitioner by applying multiplying Factor-2 in place of Factor-1 on Batukbhai Amarshibhai Vamja vs State Of Gujarat on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/67471736/
1 re-computation of the compensation in accordance with the provisions of Section 26(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 along with other statutory benefits including solatium.
2. Ms. Manvi Damle, learned counsel, holding brief of Mr. Maulik G. Nanavati, learned counsel appearing for NHAI, would point out NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/1431/2025 ORDER DATED:
06/02/2025 undefined that as per the statement made in para-3.1 of the writ petition, the petitioner is left with no right or interest in the land-in-question, inasmuch as the petitioner and other persons have sold the land in plots to several other persons.

sentences.text: It is pointed out that neither the description of the sale deeds is on record nor the purchasers to whom the land-in-question has been sold are arrayed as respondents in the present petition.
In absence of any description with respect to the sale effected by the petitioner himself, he cannot seek the relief herein.

3. Noticing the above, we may simply record the statement made by the petitioner in para 3.1 of the writ petition, which is as under:-
"3.1.

The Petitioner states and submits that on the date of declaration of intention in view of Section 3A of the National Highways Act and on the date of passing of the award under Section 3G of the Act, the land was Non-Agricultural land and was falling within Rural Area.
The Petitioner and others had sold the land in plots to several persons.
Therefore, the purchasers of the plots became the owners of the land and pertains to that several entries were made and same were certified in favour of the purchasers.

The present Petition is preferred by the Petitioner as the name of the Petitioner and others were mentioned in Notifications published under Section 3A and 3D of the Act and also in the award passed under Section 3G of the Act.

The present Petition is preferred as the name of the Petitioner is mentioned in the acquisition proceedings and there is no dispute between the Petitioner and others about the apportionment of amount of compensation.

The Petitioner has no objection if the amount of compensation is disbursed by the authorities in accordance with law."
4.

Taking note of the above, we find that the petitioner is left with no legal right or interest in the land-in-question to seek compensation by multiplication of Factor-2 on the premise that in notification under Sections 3A and 3D and the award under Section 3G, his name was reflected, that too without impleading the persons to whom the right has been transferred by the petitioner.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/1431/2025 ORDER DATED: 06/02/2025 undefined 5.
The writ petition is accordingly DISMISSED being misconceived.
